Admin doesn't display properly unicode chars in JSONFields.
Description
	 
		(last modified by ZhaoQi99)
	 
>>> import json
>>> print json.dumps('中国')
"\u4e2d\u56fd"
json.dumps use ASCII encoding by default when serializing Chinese.
So when we edit a JsonField which contains Chinese character in Django admin,it will appear in ASCII characters.
I have try to fix this this problem in ​https://github.com/adamchainz/django-mysql/pull/714.And it works prefectly.

</pr_description>

The PR description is about Django admin not displaying Unicode characters properly in JSONFields. The issue is that `json.dumps` uses ASCII encoding by default, so Chinese characters (and other non-ASCII Unicode) get escaped to their ASCII representations (e.g., `\u4e2d\u56fd` instead of `中国`).

Let me find the relevant code in Django's codebase.

django/contrib/admin/widgets.py

django/forms/utils.py:58:        return json.dumps(self.get_json_data(escape_html))
django/forms/utils.py:111:        return json.dumps(self.get_json_data(escape_html))
django/forms/fields.py:1261:        return json.dumps(value, cls=self.encoder)
django/forms/fields.py:1269:            json.dumps(initial, sort_keys=True, cls=self.encoder) !=
django/forms/fields.py:1270:            json.dumps(self.to_python(data), sort_keys=True, cls=self.encoder)
The fix is to add `ensure_ascii=False` to the `json.dumps` call in `prepare_value` so that Unicode characters are displayed properly in the admin form.
